blocks.x: What IoT, Twin & Robotics changes inside Insurance & Risk: the processes we target, the controls we inherit, the platforms underneath, and the measured delta at every gate.

In Insurance & Risk, iot, digital twin & robotics bridges the physical and digital enterprise: industrial sensor network, digital twin platforms, computer vision and edge ai, predictive maintenance, robotics and autonomous systems integration, connected products, and smart infrastructure. That is the baseline pattern; the differentiator is what it connects to: industrial iot & sensor network, digital twin platform engineering, computer vision & edge ai — delivered on Dataq Twinverse and Dataq Nexus with the sector's regulatory posture built in.

items: Claims intake drowning in documents

FNOL packets, medical reports, repair estimates and police files arrive as unstructured documents; manual triage queues claims for days before an adjuster sees them. Leakage and customer patience both bleed in the queue.
Pricing sophistication outrunning governance

GLM-based pricing, telematics factors and external data enrichment multiply model complexity faster than validation capacity. Filings get challenged; model risk documentation is reconstructed under exam pressure.
Claims, policy and exposure data fragmented
Underwriting, claims and finance each hold their own truth; loss triangles reconcile by spreadsheet. Portfolio analytics that should steer the cycle take months of manual assembly.

blocks.x: Two regimes anchor the control design here: EIOPA / state DOIs AI guidance and AML/CTF obligations. Premium and payout channels under financial-crime monitoring. Evidence for both is generated by the delivery itself — control tests, replay trails and documentation are artifacts of the program, not a reconstruction project.

This capability runs on the cadence set out below; the rhythm is fixed, the scope is signed. Weeks 1–2 measure and sign the baseline with your team; nothing builds against an unsigned number. Weeks 3–8 prove the pattern on deliberately bounded scope — one decision path, one workflow, one plant or one portfolio — under a control owner named on your side. Weeks 9–12 industrialize what worked into runbooks, monitoring and enablement, closing with a measured delta against the baseline. Every gate is pass, stop or redirect, in writing.
